acceptedAnswer.text: A 2,000 lb safe sits inside the SIR band of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, so it moves under SIR — Structural Integrity Relocation — and the KIM-GS Protocol. The route, the stairs, and the floors are surveyed before move day, floor deflection is assessed against an L/360 standard, the emptied safe is protected and moved with equipment matched to the project, and it is placed and verified with you. The price is one flat rate in writing before anything is lifted.

mainEntity.name: How do you move a gun safe that weighs 2,000 pounds?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, always. Everything comes out before move day — firearms, ammunition, documents, valuables, and loose items — so nothing shifts in transit and the load is the safe itself. Plan to transport firearms and ammunition yourself, separately, following applicable law; that is general guidance, not legal advice. When you ask for your quote, confirm the safe is empty and the lock works, because a safe that cannot be opened cannot be emptied.

mainEntity.name: Does my safe really have to be empty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — we go up and down stairs, including stairs with turns and landings. The staircase is planned step by step at the survey: step count, turns, landing size, and doorway widths at both ends, and the move itself goes one step at a time with control from above and below. If a route cannot carry the safe safely, we tell you straight and work out the route that can, before anything is attempted.

mainEntity.name: Can you carry a safe up or down a full flight of stairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is handled the same careful way, under standard heavy care — not as a lesser service. An 800 lb safe is still top-heavy and still concentrates its whole load on a few square inches of floor, so it gets the same surveyed route, the same floor check, the same protection, and the same flat rate in writing. Tell us the make, model, or approximate weight — or the size and where the safe sits — and the job is planned from there.

mainEntity.name: My safe only weighs about 800 pounds. Is it handled differently?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no published price list, because the honest price depends on the job: the safe's weight and size, the stairs and turns at both ends, the floors, whether the safe is bolted down, whether you want it re-anchored, and the distance. Once the scope is known, the whole job is reviewed and priced at one flat rate in writing — never hourly. The price you agree is the price you pay: Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free!

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to move a gun safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Re-anchoring at the destination is available on request. Say at quote time that you want it, and tell us the floor type where the safe will sit: concrete takes concrete anchors, and a wood subfloor takes lag bolts into the joists. Re-anchoring is not automatic, so it has to be in the plan before move day. If your safe is bolted down where it sits now, tell us that too, so unbolting is in the plan as well.

mainEntity.name: Will you bolt my safe down at the new house?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We do not offer locksmith services: combination changes, lock opening, and lock replacement are locksmith or manufacturer work, arranged separately by the owner before move day, and no locksmith is named or referred here. The timing matters — because the safe is always emptied first, a safe with a lock problem has to be opened before the move, not during it. Tell us the lock condition at quote time so the plan reflects a working lock.

mainEntity.name: Can you open my safe, or change its combination, while you are here?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A safe moving with the household is a common long-distance job, and the safe and the household are planned together, as one scope. Our published long-distance safe runs include Winchester to Las Vegas, and long-distance safe moves also serve collectors, dealers, and estates. Tell us From, To, the safe's weight, and the access at both ends, and the job is scoped from those facts and priced at one flat rate in writing.
